extracted.intended_audience: Wikipedia readers and contributors (researchers, journalists, general public) interested in Russian political disinformation websites
extracted.subtask_description: A Wikipedia list article that compiles websites linked to Russian political disinformation campaigns, grouped by campaign/owner, with domain, status, notes and source citations. Intended as a curated, sourced reference that editors may expand or update.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inclusion criteria for listed websites
rubrics_metrics.description: The following is a list of websites, separated by owner or disinformation campaign, that have both been considered by journalists and researchers as distributing false news - or otherwise participating in disinformation - and have been designated by journalists and researchers as likely being linked to political actors based in Russia.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Entries should only be added when journalists and researchers have considered the site as distributing false news or participating in disinformation and have designated it as likely linked to political actors based in Russia. The page notes it is a dynamic list that may never satisfy particular standards for completeness and invites editors to add missing items with references to reliable sources.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required entry fields / table columns
rubrics_metrics.description: List entries are presented with columns: Name, Domain, Status, Notes, Sources.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each website entry should include at minimum the Name and Domain, with Status (e.g., Defunct, Seized), explanatory Notes (e.g., 'Spoofs ANSA', 'Imitates Bild', or details of specific false claims), and Sources citing journalists/research reports that support the listing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sourcing standard (use of reliable sources)
rubrics_metrics.description: You can help by editing the page to add missing items, with references to reliable sources.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Additions and assertions about a site's affiliation, status, or activities must be supported by reliable sources (news outlets, research reports, official documents). The article demonstrates sourcing via footnotes to articles, reports, seizure notices and archival links; editors should follow the same practice and provide verifiable citations (archived where appropriate).

rubrics_metrics.name: Organization by owner or disinformation campaign
rubrics_metrics.description: The list is separated by owner or disinformation campaign (for example: Doppelganger, InfoRos, InfoBrics, GRU-linked lists, Portal Kombat, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Group sites under the campaign or owner to which researchers/journalists have linked them. Use campaign headings only when there is source-backed attribution of common control, coordination, or a named campaign.

rubrics_metrics.name: Status annotation and explanatory notes
rubrics_metrics.description: Status column and Notes provide contextual annotations such as 'Defunct', 'Seized by the United States federal government in 2024', 'Spoofs ANSA', 'Imitates Bild', and short explanations (e.g., fabricated article claims, impersonation targets).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Annotate notable operational states (seized, defunct), legal actions, and the nature of the deception (spoofing/imitation, false claims). Notes should briefly explain the significance and link to supporting sources; include dates and specific incidents where relevant (as the page does with seizure dates and notable fabricated stories).

rubrics_metrics.name: Attribution/classification language
rubrics_metrics.description: Listings use cautious language attributing findings to 'journalists and researchers' and often indicate links as 'have been linked by researchers' or 'designated by journalists and researchers as likely being linked to political actors based in Russia.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use attribution phrasing that reflects the source: e.g., 'linked by researchers to [campaign/actor]', 'considered by journalists as distributing false news', rather than asserting undisputed facts without sources. Maintain provenance (who made the attribution) in the entry and provide the source(s) for that attribution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Completeness disclaimer and collaborative editing guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: This article contains dynamic lists that may never be able to satisfy particular standards for completeness. You can help by editing the page to add missing items, with references to reliable sources.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognize the list is dynamic and likely incomplete; contributors should improve coverage by adding sourced entries and avoiding original research. Where completeness cannot be achieved, prioritize verifiability and reliable sourcing over exhaustive coverage.
